content:
After launching its username reservation system a few days ago, WhatsApp is now beginning to enable the full feature for some users. Here are the details.

WhatsApp begins activating reserved usernames

Last month, WhatsApp rolled out a username reservation system, allowing users to claim a unique handle ahead of the official launch of the full feature.

Users can go to "Settings" > "Account" > "Username" to claim their username, and can choose whether to allow anyone who knows it to contact you, or to require new contacts to enter an additional four-digit PIN code along with the username.

If the chosen username matches an existing account on another Meta platform (such as Facebook or Instagram), users may need to prove they have control over that corresponding account. The move aims to curb the abuse of well-known usernames and the impersonation that could be exploited for scams.

That said, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now starting to activate reserved usernames for a small number of accounts.

Users included in this first phase of rollout can now see a banner at the top of their chat list, indicating that their username has been activated and can be shared with new contacts.

The report notes that the feature is being pushed to both Beta testers and users on the stable version of WhatsApp, but emphasises that it currently appears to be limited to "very few users".

To check whether your account has been activated, look for a relevant banner at the top of your chat list, or go to the "Username" section in your profile settings. That field will tell you whether your username is active, or display a message such as "Username coming soon — we'll let you know when it's ready".
